bull.thesis: Verizon maintains a stable credit profile backed by solid operating profitability, strong interest coverage, and substantial cash generation. Its strong liquidity buffers and largely fixed-rate debt structure provide reliable protection for debt holders.

points.text: Solid interest coverage of 7.11x supported by strong underlying earnings.
High fixed-rate debt portfolio composition at 79% protects cash flows.
Robust Q2 2026 results generated free cash flow of $6.43 billion.

bear.thesis: Verizon carries a significant total debt burden with heavy near-term maturities that present ongoing refinancing risks. High balance sheet leverage limits financial flexibility alongside ongoing corporate restructuring.

points.text: Substantial total debt burden standing at $158.2 billion in 2025.
Heavy near-term maturities with $17.3 billion coming due in 2026.
Cost cutting involved eliminating approximately 500 corporate jobs and store sales.

lines.text: That $31 billion in total immediate liquidity looks much thinner when you realize Verizon faces a heavy wall of maturities right after 2026.
